clue.text: Leave roll up, avoiding onset of smoker's trouble

parts.note: to furl a flag or sail is to roll it up

indicators.note: avoiding the onset means the opening letter of the trouble is dropped

parts.note: a cough is the classic complaint of a heavy smoker

explanation.surface: A smoker is told to stop rolling cigarettes and leave before the hacking starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like a verb but is the noun: a period of absence from duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlough is a period of authorised absence from work or military duty, a synonym for leave as a noun.

clue.text: Improvement to film classifications read out

parts.note: U is the British film rating for universal viewing
PG is the parental guidance film rating

indicators.note: out here means wrong, out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recites the film ratings as a better system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read out' looks like speech, but 'out' scrambles READ into RADE.
explanation.definitionFit: An upgrade is a move to a better level or version, a form of improvement.

indicators.note: something unravelled is undone and tangled, so these letters are re-sorted

explanation.surface: A small first tug undoes some knitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unravelled' scrambles INITIALPULL.
explanation.definitionFit: From Swift's tiny people of Lilliput, the word means minute or very small.

clue.text: Forbidden to accept nothing, after raising sub

indicators.note: raising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, in reverse
to accept means the forbidden word takes in the letter for nothing

parts.note: tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A banned item is taken on board as a submarine surfaces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' puts O in TABU giving TAOBU; 'raising' turns it up. 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat is a German submarine, so it is a kind of sub.

indicators.note: the clothing hides, or obscures, the label by covering it

parts.note: hose is legwear, clothing such as stockings
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: Someone holds clothing that hides its label.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a captive held by kidnappers as security, literally one detained.

indicators.note: the blow is said to keep, that is hold within it, the word that follows

parts.note: a cuff is a light blow with the hand

explanation.surface: Someone gets a clout for missing the date they had to keep to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' looks like a disappointment, and 'keep to' like obeying the deadline; in fact 'keep' is the container signal and 'to' its contents.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-off is the point after which nothing more is accepted, the same idea as a deadline.

clue.text: Departs in carriage with soldiers, first to take revolutionary action

indicators.note: in means the departure letter sits inside the carriage

parts.note: a coupé is a closed horse-drawn carriage
D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers

indicators.note: first to means only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Leaving by coach with troops, the first to take revolutionary action.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'état is a sudden seizure of government, an overthrow of the ruling power.

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: owt is Northern English dialect for anything

explanation.surface: Anything going on? Yes, more than one thing!
explanation.walkthrough: OWT is Yorkshire dialect for anything (and NOWT for nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: The number after one is the smallest amount exceeding a single item.

clue.text: Gold is found in great excitement, as diamonds are

indicators.note: is found in means the gold sits inside the excitement

parts.note: a fever is a state of great excitement
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Gold discovered amid a frenzy, the way diamonds are.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes the Bond title 'Diamonds Are Forever'.
explanation.definitionFit: Completing the famous phrase about gems lasting eternally, the James Bond film and song title.

parts.note: the gallows was traditionally called the tree, as in 'Tyburn tree'
humour in the old sense is temperament or character

explanation.surface: A tree with a personality that is hilariously deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: the gallows was the hangman's 'tree', and humour once meant temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: Black comedy about death and disaster, joking in the face of execution, is called by this name.

clue.text: One unlikely to be converted to Taoism? Yes and no

definitions.text: One unlikely to be converted to Taoism? Yes and no

indicators.note: converted here means the letters of the Chinese creed are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A wry remark about someone resistant to taking up an Eastern religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no': a follower of Mao is unlikely to convert to Taoism religiously, yet the word TAOISM converts by rearrangement into him.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Chairman Mao's communism, officially atheist, would hardly adopt a religious path.

clue.text: Moreish, but not hearty, flavouring perhaps

indicators.note: not hearty means losing the heart, the middle letter of the word for moreish

parts.note: food that is moreish makes you want more of it, so it is addictive

explanation.surface: A food review: tasty but not substantial, perhaps the flavouring is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hearty' removes C, the central letter of ADDICTIVE. 'Moreish' is British for so tasty you want more.
explanation.definitionFit: Flavourings are one kind of substance added to food, hence an example of the general term.

indicators.note: by here means held by, so the king and consumed sit within the obsession

parts.note: to have a thing about something is to be obsessed by it
R is short for rex, king
consumed means eaten

explanation.surface: A monarch eaten up by fixation turns aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Threatening behaviour is menacing and antagonistic, so it can be described as hostile.

clue.text: Live to have fun, not a state of perplexity

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live

indicators.note: not means the word a is taken away from the word for fun

parts.note: amusement is fun or entertainment

explanation.surface: Living to enjoy yourself is no way to end up confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemusement means puzzlement or bewilderment, a condition of being perplexed.

indicators.note: the letters cause problems by getting into a mess, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a tongue, an ear became troublesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' looks like 'after' but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A following, used as a noun, is a group of attendants or supporters, a retinue.

definitions.meaning: choice as an adjective means select, excellent, uncommonly fine
a steak cooked only briefly is still red and bloody inside

explanation.surface: A grim warning that picking can turn violent.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means exceptionally good and also describes underdone meat that is still bloody.

clue.text: Wine has two sorts of appeal, in retrospect

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: IT is sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'
SA is the standard abbreviation for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A wine said to have double charm, looking back on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns ITSA round.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian white wine from Piedmont.

indicators.note: losing means the letter a is dropped from the word for fortitude

parts.note: courage is fortitude

explanation.surface: A boy's bravery as he loses a pet cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat is the cat-o'-nine-tails, a whip, not a pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, and a scourge is a whip used for punishment.

parts.note: read not as a farewell gift but as departing from the present moment

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase looks like a gift for someone leaving a job; read literally it is leaving the present for another time.
explanation.definitionFit: Journeying into past or future means quitting the current moment, the science-fiction idea of moving through the ages.

clue.text: Cross about one benefit rising? It's pleasant to the ear

indicators.note: about means the Cross goes round the other pieces

parts.note: MC is the Military Cross

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards, reversed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the dole is British unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Someone is angry at a rise in benefits, then something nice to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns IDOLE into ELODI, which the Military Cross MC goes round. 'Cross' looks like 'angry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuneful music is agreeable to listen to; melodic describes such a sound.

clue.text: Does she finally rely on men?

definitions.text: Does she finally rely on men?

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of the next word

parts.note: to lean on someone is to rely on them
OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A question about a woman's dependence on men.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a woman's name, built from the end of 'she', LEAN and OR (other ranks).
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so the clue's 'she' is a person bearing it.

parts.note: John is the name of many popes, such as John XXIII
bull is slang for nonsense

explanation.walkthrough: JOHN BULL is the cartoon personification of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The stout, beef-eating national figure is a personification of the typical Englishman.

clue.text: Advance, as one may with charges

one may bring or lay charges in a court

explanation.surface: Moving forward, as you might do with accusations.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer someone is to promote them, and one can prefer charges against an accused.

indicators.note: retains means the measure holds the letter a inside it

parts.note: a pint is a measure, perhaps of beer

explanation.surface: A beer keeps its hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint is a colouring substance; to paint is to colour.

clue.text: Sort of railway line to lose time — moreover, to stop moving

indicators.note: to lose means the letter for time is dropped from the line

parts.note: a track is a line, as of a railway
and means moreover, in addition
to pinion is to bind someone's arms so they cannot move

explanation.surface: A railway line that runs late and also comes to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR cut the clue short; the page continues it. 'Railway line' is a false pairing: the line is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack railway uses a toothed rail engaged by a cogwheel, the mechanism that gives the system its name.

indicators.note: almost means the word for manage stops one letter short

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Nearly succeeding in a capture.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop is slang for to catch or seize, as a police officer does.

indicators.note: making something fashionable restyles it, so the letters are remade
